text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prince Hassan says genuine solidarity needed to address humanitarian problems.
- Government said to be studying options for early elections.
- Crown Prince Hassan says Jordan hopes sanctions on Iraq will be lifted.
- New laws to protect state property.

- Opposition welcomes news of possibilities of early elections. Islamic Action Front (IAF) leader calls for modern elections law. IAF deputy Abdullah Akailah says participation in government is rule and not participating is exception.
- Prince Hassan calls for humanitarian charter.
- Prince Hassan follows up with concern the tragedy of two Jordanian children (who died after swallowing medicine).
- Jordan welcomes visit of Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller.

- Jordanian Trade Minister Ali Abu Al-Ragheb says his ministry is about to issue new law for foreign firms in Jordan, including measures to control regional offices and block attempts to gain exemptions.
- King Hussein to visit Qatar later this month as part of Gulf tour.
- Stocks reach highest levels since April.
- Customs department starts implementing "Green Channel" for imports of materials.
